> 寓言十九，重言十七，卮言日出，和以天倪。

寓言 nine in ten; 重言 seven in ten; 卮言 comes out daily, harmonized with the natural boundary.

This is the book explaining its own instruments, and it is the most quoted and most misread chapter in 莊子.

## 寓言: lodging a word in someone else

寓: to lodge, to entrust. 藉外論之 — to argue through something outside.

Why? Because 親父不為其子媒 — a father does not arrange his own son's marriage. 親父譽之，不若非其父者也 — a father's praise carries less weight than a stranger's.

So the device is not decoration. It is a concession to how people receive claims: the same sentence from a different mouth lands differently. 非吾罪也，人之罪也 — not my fault; theirs.

## 重言: weight, from age

重 reads zhòng: weighty, relied upon. 所以已言也 — used to put an end to talk. 是為耆艾 — this is what elders are for.

But the chapter immediately undercuts its own instrument: 年先矣，而無經緯本末 — older, yes, and without warp or weft, without beginning or end. Such a person is a 陳人 — a stale man, a man left out on display.

So 重言 is not "quote the old." It is: use what has weight, and notice when the weight is only age.

## 卮言: the vessel that tips

卮 is a wine cup. Its property: empty, it stands upright; full, it tips over.

The common reading turns this into "slippery speech," the diplomat's art. That reading is wrong, and the vessel's physics says why: the cup is not evasive. It has no fixed posture — which is precisely what lets it follow the thing in front of it.

卮言 is speech with no fixed shape, therefore able to fit.

## 天倪: the boundary that is naturally there

倪: edge, division. 和以天倪 — harmonized with the natural boundary.

Compare this with 齊物論's 封. There, boundaries were drawn by sentences and then believed. Here, the boundary is the one a thing already has. The instrument is speech without a fixed posture, fitted to a boundary it did not draw.

## 曼衍 and 窮年

因以曼衍，所以窮年 — follow it as it spreads, and so finish one's years.

A very light sentence, and a very heavy one. It describes a whole life's method: not completion, not a system, but a drift that keeps going.

## 然於然

It is so because it is so.

Not because it matches a standard. This is the smallest and most consequential sentence in the chapter: the ground of a thing being so is the thing itself, and every additional ground is a boundary someone drew.

## 始卒若環，莫得其倫

Beginning and end like a ring, no seam to be found.

## 天均: the potter's wheel

均 is the 陶鈞, the turntable on which clay is thrown.

Not a static balance. A rotation whose center holds.

## 六十而六十化

Sixty years, and sixty years of changing.

惠子's judgment of 孔子 is that he 勤志服知 — diligent in will, devoted to knowledge: still working, still acquiring. The chapter's reply is 謝之矣 — he has put it down.

## The test

Take one explanation you use for your own behavior. Then apply 然於然: is it so because it is so, or because you have installed a ground under it? Every ground beyond the first is a boundary, and boundaries get defended.
